body: I can confirm this on 4.5.beta 0dd917826 (Linux). The issue seems to go away when you disable **Fix Alpha Border** on the image in the Import dock:

Yes, it is the `fix_alpha_border` toggle, but afaik it's kind of working as it should. It just doesn't work for these kind of images. This is the result of it: Which looks as is expected when expanding the partly darker pixels of the source image... ... that are considered "edges" by the function: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/0dd9178269e447aca805bc4b4a9a840119c10275/core/io/image.cpp#L3935 When the shadow is less than the alpha threshold, the color of the lighter text will bleed on it. In this particular case, since the text sits on top of the shadow i.e. you actually want to blend towards black, the correct course of action is to disable the `fix_alpha_border`. In general though e.g. if the text had no shadow, the preferred approach for an image that is supposed to be single color is to _only_ change the alpha when blending towards transparency: Above gradient goes from transparent white to white, gradient below from transparent black to white. I do not use photoshop so I don't know how, but I'm almost certain the color of the transparent background can be changed somewhere. For the engine side, the only thing to really do is to either: 1. Nothing, as there already is a tooltip for the `fix_alpha_border` toggle that says to disable it if the image doesn't look correct. 2. Better document when exactly the toggle won't work (mostly gradients). And maybe change the language to better reflect the reality from: "_It is recommended to leave this enabled_" to more of a "_Please be aware that images still have color in transparent areas and author them with this in mind. Also premultiplied alpha is superi-_" in a little less condescending tone perhaps but indicating that "correctly" authored images should in fact disable it. 3. Expose the constant values of the function as properties (did not check if they can be): https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/0dd9178269e447aca805bc4b4a9a840119c10275/core/io/image.cpp#L3934-L3935
